item.title: Seven-year terms could delay voter accountability, critics warn
item.description: A proposal to extend the term of elected officials from five to seven years under Constitutional Amendment Bill No. 3 has raised concerns that voters may have to wait longer to hold councillors accountable for poor service delivery.

item.title: Gukurahundi testimonies reveal scale of atrocities
item.description: The government’s announcement that more than 25 000 people have given testimony in the ongoing Gukurahundi Community Outreach Programme has confirmed the vast scale of the 1980s atrocities, reflecting decades of unspoken grief, unresolved trauma with communities still grappling with the social and economic aftershocks of the violence.

item.title: Parliament invites public comments on Amendment Bill
item.description: The Parliament of Zimbabwe has invited members of the public to submit comments on the proposed Constitution of Zimbabwe Amendment (No. 3) Bill, 2026.

item.title: Why tinkering with term limits demands extreme caution
item.description: Legal experts in Zimbabwe have raised concerns about proposed constitutional changes, warning that they could weaken safeguards designed to limit executive power.

item.title: EMA, partners join hands in drive to restore Harare’s cleanliness
item.description: The Environmental Management Agency has noted with concern littering and illegal dumping of waste by residents in Harare.

item.title: UK connects Zimbabwean farmers with UK and European buyers
item.description: (Harare) – Eight buyers from the United Kingdom and European Union will visit 11 Zimbabwean farm and food businesses that have primed their horticulture products for exports through their work with the International Trade Centre (ITC). The trade mission is organised by the UK Trade Partnerships (UKTP) Programme, funded by the UK government and implemented by ITC.
